newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Former RBA gov. Fraser says economy can do better.
newsitem.headline: Former RBA gov. Fraser says economy can do better.

text.p: Former Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Bernie Fraser said on Friday the Australian economy needs to perform better than it is currently to reduce unemployment.

Speaking to reporters ahead of giving a speech, he was asked what he would be discussing in a talk to an building industry meeting, Fraser said: "Basically, what I'm going to say is we can do better than we are doing."
"We need to be doing better than we are in order to take down the unemployment rate," he said.
Fraser's seven year term as central bank governor ended in September 1996.

Australia's unemployment rate fell to 8.5 percent in June from 8.7 percent in May, but the fall was mainly due to discouraged job-seekers giving up the search for work. Unemployment has been stuck or above 8.5 percent since the Coalition government won the election in March 1996.

Analysts widely expect another cut in official interest rates later this month or in August due to the stalled labour market conditions, subdued consumer confident and an economy running below capacity.
Second quarter inflation and wages data, due next week, are expected to provide further fuel to calls for another rate cut, which would be the fifth since July 1996.
